actions.label: Reproduce Advanced Paste Foundry Local integration behavior

reproduce.expected: A usable running Foundry service should list supported cached models; an unusable endpoint should be reported as a connection/compatibility failure, not as available with no downloaded models.
steps: Use test Foundry CLI/runtime versions matching0.10,0.11and0.12reports; verify a test model through the CLI and its actual endpoint.
Trace SDK creation, endpoint discovery, model-list errors and provider IsAvailable; include an empty/unusable endpoint and service-restart control.

Verify the supported SDK/runtime integration and present a localized actionable compatibility/connection failure rather than a successful empty-model state; preserve other providers and avoid hard-coded endpoints.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.

known_information: Multiple participants report a running/downloaded model through Foundry CLI0.10to0.12but an empty PowerToys Service URL and invalid-URI errors across GPU/NPU backends.
The thread supplies diagnostic excerpts and an archive; a proposed old-CLI workaround is explicitly speculative, not a verified recommendation.

Current-main FoundryClient uses FoundryLocalManager and can return an empty endpoint; catalog/cache errors become empty lists. FoundryLocalModelProvider.IsAvailable checks only whether the client object exists after initialization.
That verifies an error/availability boundary, but not the exact internal SDK commands or which SDK version supports every newer runtime.
inferences: The proposed mechanism is provisional and is not an executed runtime result or evidence that the old report is fixed.
issue_context.summary: Investigate Foundry Local endpoint compatibility and truthful availability errors
issue_context.analysis: An initialized client object with an unusable endpoint can be reported as available while model discovery fails, masking compatibility failures as no downloaded models. Validate endpoint capability and SDK/runtime support before accepting availability; do not hard-code a port or recommend an unverified downgrade.
